title: Vanessa Van Edwards: The Conversation Habit That Makes Smart People Unlikable (Part 4)

lines.en: This is I think the most important one to talk about actually.
lines.zh: 其實我覺得這是最重要、最需要談的一種。

lines.en: I think it's the least understood of all the archetypes which is the selfless helper. Okay.
lines.zh: 我覺得它是所有原型中最不被理解的，就是「無私的助人者」。好。

lines.en: This is such a clear narrative.
lines.zh: 這是一種非常清楚的敘事。

lines.en: I almost always can predict it within the first few minutes of conversation and that is because selfless helpers their entire story is about giving.
lines.zh: 我幾乎總能在對話的頭幾分鐘就預測出來，因為無私助人者的整個故事都是關於付出。

lines.en: Their entire reason for being is being of service.
lines.zh: 他們存在的全部理由就是服務。

lines.en: They almost always pick careers that are of service.
lines.zh: 他們幾乎總是選擇服務型的職業。

lines.en: They almost always pick careers teachers, coaches, trainers, nurses, doctors.
lines.zh: 他們幾乎總是選擇老師、教練、訓練員、護理師、醫生這類職業。

lines.en: And that is because they are so ingrained that to have worth is to help.
lines.zh: 那是因為在他們心中根深蒂固地認為：有價值就是要幫助別人。

lines.en: And often times where they can sometimes get into trouble is they don't feel worthy if they are not helping.
lines.zh: 而他們有時會遇到麻煩的地方，是如果沒在幫助別人，他們就覺得自己沒有價值。

lines.en: And so they help so much that there's nothing left.
lines.zh: 所以他們幫得太多，直到什麼都不剩。

lines.en: They have compassion burnout or compassion fatigue because they are giving and giving and giving and giving. They cannot say no.
lines.zh: 他們會有同理心倦怠或同理心疲勞，因為他們一直付出、付出、付出、付出。他們沒辦法說不。

lines.en: In a relationship they are beautiful to be in a relationship with because they are givers, right?
lines.zh: 在感情中，和他們在一起非常美好，因為他們是付出者，對吧？

lines.en: They are they are nurturers. They are giving.
lines.zh: 他們是照顧者。他們很會付出。

lines.en: They're they're you know a lot of parents can flip into self-el helpers once they become a parent.
lines.zh: 你知道，很多父母一旦當了爸媽，就會轉變成無私的助人者。

lines.en: I've seen this happen with both moms and dads.
lines.zh: 我在媽媽和爸爸身上都看過這種情況。

lines.en: The moment they have a baby they flip into selfless helper cuz all of a sudden their purpose is there is to take care of this little person.
lines.zh: 他們一有了寶寶，就轉變成無私的助人者，因為突然之間他們的目的就是照顧這個小小的人。

lines.en: The problem is that they h they they have a really hard time saying no. They're people pleasers. Yeah.
lines.zh: 問題是他們很難說不。他們是討好者。對。

lines.en: They have they struggle with boundaries.
lines.zh: 他們在設立界線上很掙扎。

lines.en: They say yes to too much and they put themselves last.
lines.zh: 他們答應太多事，把自己擺在最後。

lines.en: Can be both good and bad in a relationship.
lines.zh: 在感情中可能是好事，也可能是壞事。

lines.en: And so if you're in a relationship with them, sometimes half of it is just letting them stand up to protect themselves to not give too much.
lines.zh: 所以如果你和他們在一起，有時一半的工作就是讓他們站出來保護自己，不要付出太多。

lines.en: And I mentioned this very briefly earlier, but I've had many friends who are selfless help helpers and they attract takers, right?
lines.zh: 我稍早很簡短地提過，我有很多朋友是無私的助人者，而他們會吸引索取者，對吧？

lines.en: They attract high conflict people.
lines.zh: 他們會吸引高衝突型的人。

lines.en: You know what I mean by high conflict? Oh, okay. Yeah.
lines.zh: 你知道我說的高衝突是什麼意思嗎？喔，好。對。

lines.en: A high conflict person is Bill Eddy's work.
lines.zh: 高衝突型的人是 Bill Eddy 的研究。

lines.en: He estimates that 10% of the population is a high conflict person.
lines.zh: 他估計人口中有 10% 是高衝突型的人。

lines.en: A high conflict person is someone who thrives with drama.
lines.zh: 高衝突型的人是在戲劇性衝突中如魚得水的人。

lines.en: They create difficulty in their relationships.
lines.zh: 他們會在關係中製造困難。

lines.en: They almost like to have difficult conversations.
lines.zh: 他們幾乎喜歡進行困難的對話。

lines.en: They thrive with that kind of drama. They see an absolutes.
lines.zh: 他們在那種戲劇性中如魚得水。他們用絕對的眼光看事情。

lines.en: So they often speak in like black or white.
lines.zh: 所以他們說話常常是非黑即白。

lines.en: Um they see no nuance.
lines.zh: 嗯，他們看不到細微差別。

lines.en: They weaponize emotions. these days they often sometimes use psychology to their advantage by taking advantage of people

lines.en: and the the worst high conflict people and this is where I've noticed it in my work when I was listening and reading Bill Eddy's work I was
lines.zh: 而最糟的高衝突型人，這是我在工作中注意到的，當我聽、讀 Bill Eddy 的研究時，我想：

lines.en: like they actually are enablers they can get other people to do their dirty work for them so they can sometimes put a seed in a selfless helper's ear
lines.zh: 他們其實是在唆使別人，他們能讓別人替他們做骯髒事，所以他們有時會在無私助人者耳邊種下一顆種子，

lines.en: and the selfless helper will go how dare they and they'll go fight for you and so sometimes selfless helper ers,

lines.zh: 會被捲入一些他們不一定該做的事，因為他們在替自己在乎的人挺身而出。

lines.en: And so if you're dealing with a selfless helper in terms of conversation,
lines.zh: 所以如果你在對話中面對的是無私的助人者，

lines.zh: 對，有時他們甚至覺得談論自己就是一種索取。好。

lines.zh: 所以有時在對話中，你問他們一個問題，他們會說：「喔不不，別聊我了。」對。對。對。

lines.en: Oh, let's talk about you.
lines.zh: 「喔，我們來聊你吧。

lines.en: Oh, I want to help you.
lines.zh: 喔，我想幫你。

lines.en: How can I help you?
lines.zh: 我能怎麼幫你？」

lines.en: It's so funny like my friends who are selfless helpers, I cannot get them to tell me what I can help them with cuz all they want to do is check in on me and I'm like, "No, no, I really do want to hear about you."
lines.zh: 真的很好笑，像我那些無私助人者的朋友，我沒辦法讓他們告訴我可以幫他們什麼，因為他們只想關心我，我就說：「不不，我真的想聽你的事。」

lines.en: So sometimes they won't take the ball cuz they're worried it's selfish.
lines.zh: 所以有時他們不會接球，因為他們擔心那樣很自私。

lines.en: And so sometimes getting them to open up can be hard cuz they feel like their needs are not important, but their needs are very important.
lines.zh: 所以有時要讓他們敞開心扉很難，因為他們覺得自己的需求不重要，但他們的需求非常重要。

lines.en: Like they're such beautiful people.
lines.zh: 他們是這麼美好的人。

lines.en: So I think in conversation, the greatest gift we can give a selfless helper is letting them know that you're understood. I value you.
lines.zh: 所以我覺得在對話中，我們能給無私助人者最棒的禮物，是讓他們知道：你被理解了。我重視你。

lines.en: And getting to know you is not taking from me. It's giving to me.
lines.zh: 而認識你不是在向我索取，而是在給予我。

lines.en: I have to tell my friends, it makes me feel good to help you.
lines.zh: 我得跟我的朋友說：幫助你讓我感覺很好。

lines.en: It makes me feel good to hear about what's going on for you.
lines.zh: 聽你分享你的近況讓我感覺很好。

lines.en: You're actually giving to me by telling me about yourself, not taking from me.
lines.zh: 你告訴我你的事，其實是在給予我，而不是向我索取。

lines.en: So, we have to gift to them.
lines.zh: 所以我們得給他們禮物。

lines.en: I think we have to be extremely conversationally generous with them. Mhm.
lines.zh: 我覺得我們對他們得在對話上極度慷慨。嗯。

lines.en: Do you know Do you know anyone? Yes, I do. Oh, lovely. Yeah.
lines.zh: 你認識……你認識這樣的人嗎？認識。喔，真好。對。

lines.en: And it all it all tracks with everything you said. So,
lines.zh: 而且一切都跟你說的完全吻合。所以，

lines.en: and and in corporate like right all these apply to work.
lines.zh: 而且在企業裡，對吧，這些都適用於職場。

lines.en: These are great if you have a not always but often managers can do great things as selfless helpers because they are so attuned to others but they are very good at bringing out performance.
lines.zh: 這些很棒，如果你有……不一定，但通常主管如果是無私的助人者，可以做得很出色，因為他們對別人非常敏銳，也非常擅長帶出績效。

lines.en: Not always but I've seen really really amazing managers who they know the ROI they know metrics like they're following their KPIs but they're so good at finding how does this person need to be helped?
lines.zh: 不一定，但我看過非常非常出色的主管，他們懂投資報酬率、懂數據，也追蹤 KPI，但他們非常擅長找出這個人需要什麼幫助。

lines.en: How could this person be their best selves?
lines.zh: 這個人要怎麼做到最好？

lines.en: Oh that person has a great expert power.
lines.zh: 喔，那個人有很強的專業影響力。

lines.en: They're so good at that that they bring up performance in everyone,
lines.zh: 他們太擅長這點了，所以能提升每個人的績效，

lines.en: but they might avoid the difficult conversation.
lines.zh: 但他們可能會逃避困難的對話。

lines.en: These people tend to be a little bit conflict avoidant.
lines.zh: 這些人往往有點逃避衝突。

lines.en: They can be conflict avoidant, but they're very good at framing everything as we're in this together.
lines.zh: 他們可能逃避衝突，但他們非常擅長把一切框架成「我們是一起的」。

lines.en: So yes, they can be conflict avoidant, but the really good managers who are excellent conversationalists, they are able to frame bad news and hard feedback as I want to help you.
lines.zh: 所以對，他們可能逃避衝突，但真正好的、很會溝通的主管，能把壞消息和嚴厲的回饋框架成「我想幫你」。

lines.en: Mhm. The reason I'm giving you this feedback is cuz I so want you to succeed.
lines.zh: 嗯。「我給你這個回饋的原因，是因為我非常希望你成功。」

lines.en: And the person on the receiving end goes, "I trust you. I know that." Okay.
lines.zh: 而接收的人會想：「我信任你。我知道。」好。

lines.en: So, yes, if if they're not excellent conversationalist, it's true.
lines.zh: 所以對，如果他們不是很會溝通，確實是這樣。

lines.en: They they can be avoidant.
lines.zh: 他們可能會逃避。

lines.en: But if they learn how to be assertive, and by the way, learning, you know, you can be assertive, then they are uh tremendous in conversation because they're people trust them because they come from a good place.
lines.zh: 但如果他們學會堅定表達，順帶一提，堅定表達是可以學的，他們在對話中就會非常出色，因為大家信任他們，因為他們出自善意。

lines.en: Okay. The creative disruptor. So, the creative disruptor.
lines.zh: 好。創意破壞者。所以，創意破壞者。

lines.en: This is my most challenging archetype.
lines.zh: 這是對我來說最有挑戰性的原型。

lines.en: So, I'm really going to try to talk about this archetype in a positive way.
lines.zh: 所以我真的會試著用正面的方式來談這個原型。

lines.en: Creative disruptors do not like rules.
lines.zh: 創意破壞者不喜歡規則。

lines.en: Their entire ethos is breaking things. They want to disrupt.
lines.zh: 他們的整個精神就是打破東西。他們想要顛覆。

lines.en: They want to go anti-norm.
lines.zh: 他們想反常規。

lines.en: They want to be countercultural.
lines.zh: 他們想反主流文化。

lines.en: They're the ones who are like, I don't need a blueprint.
lines.zh: 他們就是那種會說：我不需要藍圖的人。

lines.en: And they them and me in conversation is is not always the best.
lines.zh: 而他們和我在對話中不一定是最合拍的。

lines.en: There are probably the ones in the com comments who are like, "Well, this doesn't apply to me because of all these reasons cuz they want to push.
lines.zh: 留言區裡大概就有他們，會說：「嗯，這不適用於我，因為種種原因」，因為他們想挑戰。

lines.en: They want to challenge." And this is wonderful because they often are the really creative thinkers, right?
lines.zh: 他們想質疑。」這很棒，因為他們往往是真正有創意的思考者，對吧？

lines.en: They often are the ones who are thinking outside the box the most.
lines.zh: 他們往往是最跳脫框架思考的人。

lines.en: They're often the ones who are willing to challenge the way something has always been done.
lines.zh: 他們往往是願意挑戰一直以來做事方式的人。

lines.en: The problem is is sometimes that can rub people the wrong way.
lines.zh: 問題是有時候這會惹惱別人。

lines.en: And sometimes these folks can thrive over conflict in the way of it's just it's fun for them. like it's fun to negotiate,
lines.zh: 而有時這些人能在衝突中如魚得水，因為那對他們來說很好玩，像談判很好玩，

lines.en: it's fun to push a litigators, my litigators who are watching, I find that my my litigators tend to fall into this into this category
lines.zh: 推一把很好玩。訴訟律師們，正在看的訴訟律師們，我發現我的訴訟律師朋友往往屬於這一類，

lines.en: or very disruptive entrepreneurs. I I know there's ones on this show, I've listened to the interviews with them and I go, "Oh, that's a creative disruptor."
lines.zh: 或是非常具顛覆性的創業家。我知道這個節目上就有，我聽了他們的訪談，心想：「喔，那是創意破壞者。」

lines.en: It's someone who they're not only building something, but they're not quite an ambitious hero because they want to break things.
lines.zh: 那是一種人，他們不只是在打造東西，但又不太算雄心勃勃的英雄，因為他們想打破東西。

lines.en: Like, they want to build it and break it.
lines.zh: 他們想打造它，然後打破它。

lines.en: They want to reinvent the entire system, and they're doing it.
lines.zh: 他們想重新發明整個體系，而且他們真的在做。

lines.en: You know, Edward Snowden is is one of the examples I give in the book of like he he wanted to change something and also he he wanted to like stick it to the man like he wanted to break the system that he was in.
lines.zh: 你知道，Edward Snowden 是我在書裡舉的例子之一，他想改變某件事，也想對抗權威，他想打破他身處的體系。

lines.en: Mhm. H okay. Do you struggle with this?
lines.zh: 嗯。嗯，好。你會覺得這很辛苦嗎？

lines.en: Do you like this interviews? They they're very interesting.
lines.zh: 你喜歡這種訪談嗎？他們非常有意思。

lines.en: They're really good in interviews.
lines.zh: 他們在訪談中表現很好。

lines.en: I actually interviewed someone the other day that was like that. So interesting
lines.zh: 我前幾天其實就訪問了一個這樣的人。非常有意思，

lines.en: because they have a contrarian view by nature.
lines.zh: 因為他們天生就有反向的觀點。

lines.en: Everything they say is like deeply contrarian. Mhm.
lines.zh: 他們說的每件事都非常反向。嗯。

lines.en: But I think I think having people like that that are challenging around their like default is challenge is quite is quite useful. Yes.
lines.zh: 但我覺得身邊有這種預設就是挑戰的人，其實相當有用。對。

lines.en: It helps me be sort of refine my my my own points of view
lines.zh: 這幫助我精煉自己的觀點，

lines.en: It can be amazing but it can be exhausting.
lines.zh: 這可以很棒，但也可能很累。

lines.zh: 所以在對話中，最好有心理準備，知道：啊，我需要這個。

lines.en: I want to get stronger.
lines.zh: 我想變得更強。

lines.en: I want to be anti-fragile.
lines.zh: 我想變得反脆弱。

lines.en: They'll break for you to make you stronger or like I'm a delicate flower right now.
lines.zh: 他們會為了讓你更強而打破你，或是：我現在是一朵嬌嫩的花。

lines.en: I cannot do the dream killing. I'm exhausted by it.
lines.zh: 我承受不了毀夢。我被它搞得筋疲力盡。

lines.en: It's a fine line between that and like pessimism.
lines.zh: 這和悲觀之間只有一線之隔。

lines.zh: 我們有一個創意破壞者朋友，我發過一則 Instagram 貼文，我說，你知道，我有一個朋友總是說「我討厭一切」。

lines.en: Okay, the last one is one we've actually already touched on, which is the unlucky struggler.
lines.zh: 好，最後一種我們其實已經談過了，就是「不幸的掙扎者」。

lines.en: So, this is someone with a contamination narrative.
lines.zh: 這是擁有污染敘事的人。

lines.en: And they feel that no matter what they've done, they are unlucky. They are struggling. They often feel stuck. They often feel misunderstood. They often feel overlooked.
lines.zh: 他們覺得不管自己做了什麼，都很倒楣。他們在掙扎。他們常覺得卡住。他們常覺得被誤解。他們常覺得被忽視。

lines.en: And the problem with unlucky strugglers, the the the character you want to think of is like George Costanza from Seinfeld, right?
lines.zh: 不幸掙扎者的問題，你可以想到的角色像是《歡樂單身派對》裡的 George Costanza，對吧？

lines.en: Like, h everything is bad for me.
lines.zh: 像是：唉，每件事對我來說都很糟。

lines.en: They can be hilarious, but they are tortured. They are tortured.
lines.zh: 他們可能很好笑，但他們很痛苦。他們很痛苦。

lines.en: And in conversation, it's really hard for ambitious heroes to not try to convince them that they're not unlucky.
lines.zh: 而在對話中，雄心勃勃的英雄很難不去試著說服他們，他們其實不倒楣。

lines.en: Like my biggest challenge with my unlucky strugglers in my life is to not try to flip them into something that they're not or try to convince them that they're actually lucky.
lines.zh: 像我面對生活中不幸的掙扎者，最大的挑戰就是不要試著把他們翻轉成他們不是的樣子，或試著說服他們其實很幸運。

lines.en: They also in conversation can be very funny.
lines.zh: 他們在對話中也可以非常好笑。

lines.en: Like they can make fun of themselves.
lines.zh: 他們可以自嘲。

lines.en: They're so humble. their low self-esteem.
lines.zh: 他們很謙虛，自尊心低。

lines.en: Some of the best comedians are unlucky strugglers.
lines.zh: 有些最棒的喜劇演員就是不幸的掙扎者。

lines.en: And she began to tell me about his interesting stories.
lines.zh: 然後她開始跟我講他那些有趣的故事。

lines.en: She remembered his interestingness from that answer.
lines.zh: 她因為那個回答而記住了他的有趣。

lines.en: So even like where are your settings? Are you doing coffee?
lines.zh: 所以甚至你常在什麼場合？你常去喝咖啡嗎？

lines.en: Is there interesting coffee anecdotes?
lines.zh: 有沒有什麼有趣的咖啡軼事？

lines.en: Are you always at meals? Are you right?
lines.zh: 你常常在吃飯嗎？你是……對吧？

lines.en: So you can also set yourself up and them up for success with those interesting answers.
lines.zh: 所以你也可以用這些有趣的回答，讓你自己和對方都順利展開對話。

lines.en: So have a script for the questions that you get asked the most that offer gifts to those that are on the receiving end of that answer.
lines.zh: 所以要為你最常被問到的問題準備一套說法，送給接收答案的人一份禮物。

lines.en: Yeah. And the last thing I would say is this is a plan.
lines.zh: 對。我最後要說的是，這是一個計畫。

lines.en: And the entire goal of this is for you to feel more in control, for you to feel more confident.
lines.zh: 而這一切的目標，是讓你覺得更有掌控感、更有自信。

lines.en: You know, I think as someone who wasn't confident for a long time and who had very awkward conversations for a long time, just knowing that I had a good intent helped me a lot.
lines.zh: 你知道，身為一個很長一段時間沒有自信、很長一段時間對話都很尷尬的人，光是知道我有好的意圖，就幫了我很多。

lines.en: So, this is the plan.
lines.zh: 所以這就是計畫。

lines.en: But also, feel free to totally deviate from the plan.
lines.zh: 但也請隨意完全偏離計畫。

lines.en: That when you're in the moment, if you're feeling excited and and interested and engaged, go with it.
lines.zh: 當你在當下，如果你覺得興奮、有興趣、很投入，就順著走。

lines.en: If you're feeling I don't like this person, I don't feel this person, we are off, you can leave the conversation.
lines.zh: 如果你覺得我不喜歡這個人、我對這個人沒感覺、我們不合拍，你可以離開對話。

lines.en: Who did you write this book for, Vanessa?
lines.zh: Vanessa，你這本書是寫給誰的？

lines.en: So if they're, you know, if they've gotten to this stage in the conversation and they're thinking, should I get that book or not?
lines.zh: 所以如果他們，你知道，聽到對話的這個階段，正在想我該不該買這本書？

lines.en: Who is it for? This is for people who want to stop dreading small talk.
lines.zh: 它是寫給誰的？這是寫給想要不再害怕閒聊的人。

lines.en: Dread is was a real motivation for me because so many of my students would say, "Oh, I have to go to the networking event.
lines.zh: 「害怕」對我來說是真正的動力，因為我很多學生會說：「喔，我得去參加那個社交活動。

lines.en: I I'm dreading talking to my boss.
lines.zh: 我很怕跟我老闆說話。

lines.en: I hate those first five minutes of my team call.
lines.zh: 我很討厭團隊會議的前五分鐘。

lines.en: Oh, I don't know what to talk about on a date."
lines.zh: 喔，我不知道約會時要聊什麼。」

lines.en: And first dates are horrible.
lines.zh: 第一次約會很可怕。

lines.en: First dates can be fun if you have a conversational plan.
lines.zh: 如果你有對話計畫，第一次約會可以很好玩。

lines.en: Even if it's not your person, they can still be fun.
lines.zh: 就算對方不是你的人，還是可以很好玩。

lines.en: Conversation can be not awkward.
lines.zh: 對話可以不尷尬。

lines.en: It can be great at the start of a meeting if you know how to do it.
lines.zh: 如果你知道怎麼做，會議的開場可以很棒。

lines.en: And so I would like to get rid of the dread in your life.
lines.zh: 所以我想把你生活中的害怕拿掉。

lines.en: I would like to get rid of the awkwardness in your life because and the deeper meaning is we are in a loneliness epidemic.
lines.zh: 我想把你生活中的尷尬拿掉，因為更深層的意義是，我們正處在一場孤獨的流行病中。

lines.en: And I think if we don't remember how good the joy of conversation is, we won't do it.
lines.zh: 我覺得如果我們不記得對話的樂趣有多美好，我們就不會去做。

lines.en: And so if I can take away the dread of conversation and give you beautiful conversation with your person or not, you're going to feel less lonely.
lines.zh: 所以如果我能拿掉你對對話的害怕，讓你和你的人、或不是你的人有美好的對話，你就會比較不孤單。

lines.en: Kind of sounds like it's for all of us.
lines.zh: 聽起來好像是寫給我們所有人的。

lines.en: I think it's for all of us.
lines.zh: 我覺得是寫給我們所有人的。

lines.en: What a wonderful book and what a perfectly timed book at a time when AI and computers are, you know, robbing us of the joy of human conversation.
lines.zh: 多棒的一本書，而且出版的時機再完美不過，在這個 AI 和電腦正在奪走我們人際對話樂趣的時代。

lines.en: And I think increasingly kids are going to struggle with conversations.
lines.zh: 我覺得孩子們在對話上會越來越吃力。

lines.en: I mean, people are saying this already.
lines.zh: 我是說，大家已經在這樣說了。

lines.en: Teachers say to me that, you know, they see their kids in class and they don't know the basic skills of how to relate to each other through conversation.
lines.zh: 老師們跟我說，他們看到班上的孩子不知道如何透過對話和彼此互動的基本技巧。

lines.en: So, a great book I think for
lines.zh: 所以我覺得這是一本很棒的書，給……

lines.en: It was meant to be now.
lines.zh: 它注定就是現在出版。

lines.en: It was meant to be now.
lines.zh: 它注定就是現在出版。

lines.en: It was meant to be.
lines.zh: 這是注定的。

lines.en: It took you a long time, right? Yeah. Many years. 20 years. Wow.
lines.zh: 你花了很長的時間，對吧？對。很多年。20 年。哇。

lines.en: Well, I'm glad it's here.
lines.zh: 嗯，我很高興它問世了。

lines.en: Conversation: How to connect with anyone and make every interaction count.
lines.zh: 《Conversations：如何與任何人連結，讓每一次互動都有意義》。

lines.en: And I'm going to link it below if anyone wants to go and buy it right now. Thank you.
lines.zh: 如果有人現在想去買，我會把連結放在下面。謝謝你。

lines.en: What a wonderful book, Vanessa. Congratulations. Oh my goodness. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. It's finally here.
lines.zh: 多棒的一本書，Vanessa。恭喜。天啊。謝謝你。謝謝你。謝謝你。它終於問世了。

lines.en: Thank you for helping me bring it into the world. It's okay. You You deserve everything. You're such a phenom.
lines.zh: 謝謝你幫我把它帶到這個世界上。沒什麼。你值得一切。你真的是個奇才。

lines.en: My gosh, I hardly I'm obsessed with people. That's it.
lines.zh: 天啊，我幾乎……我對人很著迷。就這樣。

lines.en: We have a closing tradition where the last guest leaves a question for the next guest, not knowing who they're leaving it for.
lines.zh: 我們有一個結尾傳統，由上一位來賓留一個問題給下一位，他們不知道問題會留給誰。

lines.en: And the question left for you is, do you feel like there are things you sacrificed in your personal life to build your success that you regret and wish you could now get back?
lines.zh: 留給你的問題是：你覺得你是否為了打造成功，在個人生活中犧牲了一些東西，讓你後悔、希望現在能拿回來？

lines.en: Yes. Um, you know, I briefly mentioned that I moved and I moved to be closer to family.
lines.zh: 有。嗯，你知道，我稍早簡短提到我搬家了，我搬家是為了離家人近一點。

lines.en: Um, and that was because I think I sacrificed friendship and family relationship in the hustle.
lines.zh: 嗯，那是因為我覺得我在拚命工作的過程中，犧牲了友情和家人關係。

lines.en: You know, we moved to Austin for for work.
lines.zh: 你知道，我們為了工作搬到奧斯汀。

lines.en: I moved to Austin for work and I left my family and I I don't regret Austin cuz I had some great growth there, but I regret being away from my family when my children were very very little.
lines.zh: 我為了工作搬到奧斯汀，離開了我的家人，我不後悔去奧斯汀，因為我在那裡有很棒的成長，但我後悔在孩子還非常非常小的時候遠離家人。

lines.en: It was really hard to have babies without my mom, without my sister.
lines.zh: 沒有我媽媽、沒有我姊姊在身邊生小孩，真的非常辛苦。

lines.en: And so I wish I could have figured that out a little bit differently, but I'm here now.
lines.zh: 所以我希望當時能用稍微不同的方式處理，但我現在在這裡了。

lines.en: And what is it you wish you could get back?
lines.zh: 那你希望能拿回的是什麼？

lines.en: I felt very alone as a new mom, and I don't think that helped me or my children.
lines.zh: 身為新手媽媽，我覺得非常孤單，我不覺得那對我或我的孩子有幫助。

lines.en: I wish I could get back at time to feel more communal.
lines.zh: 我希望能拿回那段時間，讓自己更有群體的支持。

lines.en: You know, having a baby is such a beautiful thing for family and friends.
lines.zh: 你知道，生孩子對家人和朋友來說是一件非常美好的事。

lines.en: And it was it was very lonely cuz I just didn't have a lot of people around me. And now you're here.
lines.zh: 而那段時間非常孤單，因為我身邊就是沒什麼人。而現在你在這裡了。

lines.en: I know. by the beach in LA. I'm back.
lines.zh: 我知道。在洛杉磯的海邊。我回來了。

lines.en: My sister is at my house right now. Oh, really? With my kids. Yes.
lines.zh: 我姊姊現在就在我家。喔，真的嗎？和我的孩子們在一起。對。

lines.en: It's good to have you in town. I'm so excited.
lines.zh: 很高興你來到這座城市。我好興奮。

lines.en: And I will come maybe. I don't believe you.
lines.zh: 也許我會過去。我不相信你。

lines.en: You don't have to say it.
lines.zh: 你不用說。

lines.en: You don't have to say it.
lines.zh: 你不用說。

lines.en: I'm not going to invite you to anything.
lines.zh: 我不會邀請你參加任何事的。

lines.en: Conversation, how to connect with anyone and make every interaction count.
lines.zh: 《Conversations：如何與任何人連結，讓每一次互動都有意義》。

lines.en: Please do go buy this book.
lines.zh: 請務必去買這本書。

lines.en: Very important to Vanessa and also very important to me by way of that.
lines.zh: 這對 Vanessa 非常重要，因此對我也非常重要。

lines.en: And it's a brilliant, brilliant book.
lines.zh: 這是一本非常非常出色的書。

lines.en: One I think that we all need. Vanessa, thank you. We're done. Thank you. Thanks.
lines.zh: 我覺得是我們都需要的一本書。Vanessa，謝謝你。錄完了。謝謝。謝謝。
